ALLOCATION_COLLISION_SWEEP.method: A STRUCTURAL sweep over every tracked file (git ls-files), distinguishing an ALLOCATION POSITION from a mere literal occurrence. An allocation position is a parsed-JSON member whose KEY is one of GRANT_ID, authorityId, grant_id, authority_id, controller_id, node_id, artifact_id, version and whose VALUE is exactly the candidate id - never a substring in prose, never a bare array element. A literal sweep over raw bytes was run alongside it, and every literal hit was classified by reading its containing clause.
ALLOCATION_COLLISION_SWEEP.why_the_two_sweeps_are_both_needed: A value-exact sweep that ignored key position would count prohibition-list array elements as allocations. A key-position sweep alone would report ZERO and prove nothing about whether the id is discussed elsewhere. Reporting both, and classifying every literal, is what makes the negative non-vacuous.
ALLOCATION_COLLISION_SWEEP.limitation_disclosed: The structural walker parses JSON only. scripts/ods-scope.ts is TypeScript and its PROTECTED_GRANTS rows were therefore enumerated separately, by extracting the array literal and reading each authorityId. That enumeration is the grant_state.registered_ids_in_array_order list above and is what establishes that no row carries HPO-ODS-W2-28.

protected_grant.ORDER_IS_BINDING: The three patterns are stated in the order above and MUST be registered in that order. Order is part of the row identity because the registration control asserts the row with a whole-object equality, not a set comparison.
protected_grant.BRANCH_BINDING_IS_EXACT: The bound branch is the exact string codex/customer-lifecycle-cl1-implementation-r1. Resolution is by exact string equality, never by prefix, pattern or family. This branch does not exist at START_HEAD - measured across local and remote refs, where the only customer-lifecycle branches present are the PR143 authoring branch and its four audit branches - which is correct and expected: the grant is declared before the implementation branch is cut.
protected_grant.BRANCH_NAME_IS_AN_IMPLEMENTATION_CHOICE_: The Customer Lifecycle authority carries NO FUTURE_IMPLEMENTATION_BRANCH key - unlike the Packet B authority, which does. The branch name is therefore not inherited from a parent authority; it is CHOSEN by this allocation, in the shape the two most recent implementation lanes use (codex/commercial-account-ce1-implementation-r1, codex/fibdb052-p1-implementation-r1). It is binding from the moment this artifact is integrated.
protected_grant.STOP_FOR_GRANT_BRANCH_MISMATCH: If the CL-1 implementation is ever attempted from a branch whose name is not byte-identical to the bound branch, the grant contributes zero patterns, the protected write is refused, and the mission STOPS. A gate that refuses is the control working, not an obstacle to route around. Renaming the branch to match, or rebinding the grant to the branch that happens to exist, are both PROHIBITED without a governed successor.

R1_MEASUREMENT_DEFECT.classification: MEASUREMENT_METHOD_DEFECT, self-reported. Two independent misreadings of one `git show --stat` output.
R1_MEASUREMENT_DEFECT.defect_1_the_count: R1 piped `git show --stat` through a grep on the literal `prepared/journal`. `--stat` ABBREVIATES long paths, replacing a leading path segment with an ellipsis, so the `db/prepared/journal/` prefix is absent from most rows. The grep therefore matched only the 27 rows short enough to retain the prefix, and R1 reported the visible count. 54 of the 81 journal rows were invisible to the filter. The file list itself was NOT truncated - all 96 rows were printed - so this is path abbreviation, not list truncation.
R1_MEASUREMENT_DEFECT.defect_2_the_lines: `--stat` renders `| 2 +-` for a path with 1 insertion and 1 deletion, because that column is insertions PLUS deletions. R1 read that 2 as two changed lines. It is ONE line rewritten.
R1_MEASUREMENT_DEFECT.the_rule: For any claim about WHICH paths changed or HOW MANY lines, use `--numstat`: separate insertion and deletion columns, full unabbreviated paths, no ellipsis. `--stat` is a human summary and is unsafe as a measurement input, and it is unsafe in a way that fails SILENTLY - a grep over abbreviated paths returns a smaller number, never an error.
R1_MEASUREMENT_DEFECT.what_did_NOT_change: The grant shape. Both corrected figures are LARGER than the R1 figures and point the same way: 80 pre-existing wrappers move rather than 29, which strengthens rather than weakens the case that db/prepared/journal/** must be the glob. No allocation identity, pattern or branch binding is affected.

WHY_db_prepared_journal_MUST_BE_THE_GLOB.REVISION: CORRECTED AT R2. The R1 figure of twenty-nine wrappers at two lines each is WITHDRAWN and replaced by the re-measured figures below. See DIRECT_CAUSAL_EVIDENCE.R1_MEASUREMENT_DEFECT.
WHY_db_prepared_journal_MUST_BE_THE_GLOB.measured: The CE-1 commit modified EIGHTY pre-existing db/prepared/journal/*.sql wrappers - ONE line each - in addition to adding its own, for 81 journal paths in total. The P1 commit did the same to its own set: 81 pre-existing modified at one line each, plus one new, for 82 journal paths.
WHY_db_prepared_journal_MUST_BE_THE_GLOB.mechanism: Each wrapper header carries the literal Unit <ordinal>/<BASELINE_UNITS.length>, stamped by db/hosted/baseline-journal-wrapper.ts:211. Adding a baseline unit increments the denominator, which rewrites that one header line in EVERY pre-existing wrapper. This is a GENERATED-ARTIFACT REGENERATION, not an edit of unrelated files.
WHY_db_prepared_journal_MUST_BE_THE_GLOB.consequence: A grant naming only the single new wrapper path would refuse EIGHTY-ODD regenerated siblings and the mission would STOP on a scope violation it cannot lawfully route around. The glob is therefore the MINIMUM sufficient pattern, not a convenience widening.
WHY_db_prepared_journal_MUST_BE_THE_GLOB.why_the_corrected_figure_matters_even_th: At twenty-nine the glob looked like a judgement call about proportion. At eighty it is the only constructible pattern: enumerating eighty literal paths that will be eighty-one next time is not a grant, it is a stale list. The corrected measurement makes the same conclusion structural rather than discretionary.

protected_grant.NO_DB_PREPARED_WIDENING: BINDING. The prepared-surface patterns are the narrow db/prepared/journal/** and the single literal db/prepared/checkpoint-b0/observation.sql - NEVER a blanket db/prepared/**. The DEFAULT protected pattern in scripts/ods-scope.ts is the broad db/prepared/**, and the breadth of the PROTECTION is not a licence for breadth in the GRANT. A blanket grant would additionally authorize db/prepared/hosted/** and db/prepared/hosted/governed/**, which are G2-gated apply surfaces CL-1 has no business touching, and db/prepared/stella_*.sql, a separate numbering family CL-1 does not extend. A sibling under db/prepared/ that matches the default pattern but not these narrower patterns is correctly refused.
protected_grant.why_the_unprotected_entries_are_listed_a: db/policies/**, scripts/ods-controller.ts, scripts/ods-scope.ts and the two ODS test files are NOT members of DEFAULT_PROTECTED_PATTERNS and therefore need no grant to be written. They are named in the prohibition list so that no reader infers, from their absence, that the grant was silently understood to cover them. Naming a path in a prohibition is never an allocation and never a grant. db/policies/** in particular is named because the CL-1 RLS work could plausibly be mistaken for belonging there: it does NOT. The measured precedent for an audit_logs INSERT policy is a MIGRATION - 0042 and 0067 - not a db/policies unit. scripts/ods-scope.ts is named because it is where the W2-28 REGISTRATION act will land, and that act is explicitly not authorized here.
protected_grant.grant_does_not_replace_allow: The grant widens what the bound branch MAY write; it does not populate the mission --allow list. The implementing mission must still derive its own --allow list from its own measured diff at its own base, and a protected path in that diff that this grant does not cover is a SCOPE DELTA requiring adjudication - never a silent addition on the ground that it changed anyway.

UNPROTECTED_SURFACES_CL1_WILL_ALSO_TOUCH.status: INFORMATIVE, NOT A GRANT. Every path below is OUTSIDE DEFAULT_PROTECTED_PATTERNS and needs an --allow entry, never a grant. Listing them here prevents the implementing mission from reading the grant as the whole of its write surface.
UNPROTECTED_SURFACES_CL1_WILL_ALSO_TOUCH.measured_basis: The CE-1 commit touched db/schema.ts and db/hosted/baseline-manifest.ts alongside its protected paths; the P1 commit touched db/schema.ts and six test files. Both sets are unprotected.
UNPROTECTED_SURFACES_CL1_WILL_ALSO_TOUCH.NOT_AN_AUTHORIZATION: This list does not authorize any of these paths. It records which of them are unprotected so that the implementing mission derives an --allow list rather than assuming the grant covers everything it needs.

protected_grant.why_existing_grants_cannot_be_reused: MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED. Seven registered grants carry the db/migrations/** or db/prepared/journal/** families - W2-01, W2-12, W2-17, W2-20 with W2-21, W2-25, W2-26 and W2-27 - and four carry db/prepared/checkpoint-b0/observation.sql: W2-07, W2-16, W2-17 and W2-26. Every one of them is bound to a DIFFERENT branch. Resolution is by exact branch equality, so on codex/customer-lifecycle-cl1-implementation-r1 all of them contribute zero patterns. A new row is therefore doing real work and is not a duplicate of an existing grant.

MIGRATION_ORDINAL_DISPOSITION.POSTURE: B - NO ORDINAL IS ALLOCATED. Permission is granted for the implementing lane to derive the ordinal at its own exact implementation HEAD, by the normal drizzle-kit generate path.
MIGRATION_ORDINAL_DISPOSITION.why_posture_B_and_not_A: This is not a choice made by this lane; it is the pattern ODS authority has already established and the only one the record supports. v1.0.30 NO_PREALLOCATION.migration_ordinal_disposition sets allocated false, reserved false, implied false, records the first free candidate as a DATED OBSERVATION and imposes a re_measurement_obligation in exactly these terms. The Customer Lifecycle authority independently requires the same thing from the other direction: LINEAGE_REDERIVATION_REQUIRED is YES, scope EVERY object without exception, on the measured ground that the tail moved from 0067 to 0069 within the span of the authorities it consumes and that CE-1 own forward reference to 0068 was already stale at its AS_OF_TREE. Two independent frozen authorities converge on posture B.
MIGRATION_ORDINAL_DISPOSITION.candidate_derivation: The highest existing db/migrations/NNNN_*.sql ordinal at START_HEAD is 0069_fib_fibdb052_p1_indexes.sql and db/migrations/meta/_journal.json holds max idx 69 across 70 entries. 0070 is therefore the first free candidate AT THIS HEAD.
MIGRATION_ORDINAL_DISPOSITION.THIS_IS_NOT_A_RESERVATION: BINDING. 0070 is recorded as a DATED OBSERVATION and nothing more. It is not allocated, not reserved, and confers no entitlement. Concurrent lanes may land a migration between this artifact and the implementing mission, and reading 0070 off 0069 here and carrying it forward would be exactly the stale-count inheritance the authority chain forbids. At least four sibling authorities - async, PVRI, wave4 and the commercial state authority - are live and each has explicitly disclaimed 0070 rather than taken it, which is the measured reason this window is real rather than theoretical.
MIGRATION_ORDINAL_DISPOSITION.re_measurement_obligation: The migration ordinal MUST be re-measured by the implementing mission at its OWN live head and produced by the normal drizzle-kit generate path. It is not computed by this artifact.
MIGRATION_ORDINAL_DISPOSITION.uniqueness_proof_not_required_because_no: The governing mission brief requires a uniqueness proof against BOTH migrations and prepared migrations IF a specific ordinal is allocated. risks_and_open_findings.finding: Two R1 measurement defects and one R1 authority-retrieval defect, all corrected at R2, all recorded because the mechanisms are reusable.
items: git show --stat abbreviates long paths, so a grep on a directory prefix silently under-counts; and its single changed-lines column is insertions PLUS deletions. Use --numstat. See protected_grant.WHY_THREE_PATTERNS_AND_NOT_TWO.DIRECT_CAUSAL_EVIDENCE.R1_MEASUREMENT_DEFECT.

A count attached to a named token must count THAT token; R1 ran a two-token alternation, counted lines, and reported it as a count of one token. See risks_and_open_findings F-CC-3.COUNT_CORRECTED_AT_R2.

When a predecessor authority in the same lineage has already frozen a census of the same objects, CONSUME and RE-MEASURE it rather than authoring a parallel one. See MEASURED_TEST_PINS_THE_IMPLEMENTING_MISSION_WILL_MOVE.R1_INVENTORY_DEFECT.
risks_and_open_findings.what_survived_unchanged: Every allocation identity, the grant shape, the branch binding, the migration-ordinal posture and the collision result. All three defects were in EVIDENCE PRECISION and in the AUTHORIZATION SURFACE handed forward, not in the allocation.

risks_and_open_findings.finding: HPO-ODS-W2-28 is DECLARED here and NOT REGISTERED. CL-1 cannot lawfully write a protected path until a separate governed act adds the row to scripts/ods-scope.ts and updates the length pin in tests/ods/ods-scope.test.ts.
risks_and_open_findings.why_this_is_by_design: Allocation and registration are separate governed acts throughout this lineage. v1.0.30 declared W2-27 as DECLARED_NOT_REGISTERED and its registration landed in a later mission.
